results.title: Odd core of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The odd core $O(G)$ of a group $G$ is the supremum, in the lattice of subgroups of $G$, of all normal subgroups of $G$ whose order is finite and odd.

results.title: Brauer–Suzuki theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $O(G)$, the odd core of $G$, be the subgroup generated by all normal subgroups of $G$ of odd order, let $n \ge 3$, and let $P$ be a Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$ isomorphic to the generalized quaternion group $Q_{2^n}$ of order $2^n$. If $t \in P$ has order $2$, then the image of $t$ in $G / O(G)$ lies in the center of $G / O(G)$.

results.title: Uniform quadratic bound on the explicit Euler local error
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space, let $t_0 < T$ be real numbers, let $f : \mathbb{R} \times E \to E$ be $C^2$, and let $x : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be differentiable at every $t \in [t_0, T]$ with $x'(t) = f(t, x(t))$. Then there is a constant $C \ge 0$ such that $\|x(t + h) - (x(t) + h f(t, x(t)))\| \le C h^2$ for every $h \in (0, T - t_0]$ and every $t \in [t_0, T]$ with $t + h \le T$.

results.title: Local truncation error of the explicit Euler method
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real Banach space, let $t_0 < T$, let $f : \mathbb{R} \times E \to E$ be $C^2$, let $x_0 \in E$, and let $x : \mathbb{R} \to E$ satisfy $x(t_0) = x_0$ and $x'(t) = f(t, x(t))$ for every $t \in [t_0, T]$. Then there is a constant $C$ such that $\|x(t + h) - (x(t) + h f(t, x(t)))\| \le C h^2$ for every $h \in (0, T - t_0]$ and every $t \in [t_0, T]$ with $t + h \le T$.

results.title: Overlaps in words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite word $o$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ is an overlap if $o = xyxyx$ for some finite words $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$ with $x$ nonempty; $y$ may be empty.

results.title: Overlap-free binary words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite binary word is overlap-free when none of its contiguous factors is an overlap.

results.title: Variable layout of the transition clauses
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A layout consists of four natural numbers derived from the verifier: the size $A$ of the label/state block of a row, the number $K$ of stacks, the number $g$ of symbol codes (code $0$ is the empty cell), and the window depth $d$.

results.title: Variables per time step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a layout with label/state block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and a height $H$, the row width is $W = A + K \cdot (H \cdot g)$: the label/state block of $A$ variables, followed by $K \cdot H \cdot g$ cell variables.

results.title: Number of variables of the transition-clause formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a layout $L$ and bounds $T$ and $H$, the number of variables is $V = (T + 1) \cdot W$, where $W$ is the number of variables per time step at height $H$.

results.title: Index of a label/state variable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For height $H$, time $t$ and $a \in \mathbb{N}$, the index of label/state variable $a$ at time $t$ is $t \cdot W + a$, where $W$ is the row width (variables per time step) at height $H$. It is used for $a < A$, the size of the label/state block.

results.title: Index of a cell variable in the transition-family layout
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a layout $L$ with label/state block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, and natural numbers $H$, $t$, $k$, $j$, $x$, the variable for stack $k$, depth $j$ from the top and symbol code $x$ at time $t$ has index $tW + A + (kH + j)g + x$, where $W = A + KHg$ is the number of variables per time step. It is meant for $k < K$, $j < H$ and $x < g$ but is defined for all values.

results.title: Number of literals of a transition clause
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a layout $L$ with $KK$ stacks and window depth $d$, a label-transition clause has $KK \cdot d + 2$ literals: the current label, the $KK \cdot d$ window cells and the next label.

results.title: Dense clause from a list of literals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given $V \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $\ell$ of pairs $(p, b)$ of a variable index $p$ and a sign $b$, the dense clause over $V$ variables has, for each $v < V$, slot $v$ equal to the literal $x_v$ if the first pair in $\ell$ with index $v$ is $(v, \mathrm{true})$, the literal $\neg x_v$ if it is $(v, \mathrm{false})$, and empty if $\ell$ has no pair with index $v$. Pairs with index at least $V$ are ignored.

results.title: Increasing literal positions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $\mathit{lo}, V \in \mathbb{N}$, a list of literals $(p_1, b_1), \dots, (p_n, b_n)$ with positions $p_k \in \mathbb{N}$ and signs $b_k$ has increasing literal positions from $\mathit{lo}$ below $V$ when $\mathit{lo} \le p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_n < V$; for the empty list ($n = 0$) the condition is $\mathit{lo} \le V$.

results.title: Lowering the lower bound keeps a literal list increasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $lo' \le lo$ and $V$ and a list $ls$ of literals, if the positions in $ls$ are strictly increasing, at least $lo$ and below $V$ (with $lo \le V$ if $ls$ is empty), then the same holds with $lo'$ in place of $lo$.

results.title: Encoding a dense clause block by block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\ell = [(p_1, b_1), \dots, (p_n, b_n)]$ be a list of literals with $p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_n < V$. Then the bit encoding of the dense clause over $V$ variables with literals $\ell$ is the gap encoding of $\ell$ from slot $0$ to $V$, followed by the clause terminator $00$.

results.title: Shifting the start of a gap encoding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \le m'$ and let $\ell = [(p_1, b_1), \dots, (p_n, b_n)]$ be a list of literals with $m' \le p_1 < \dots < p_n < V$ (if $\ell$ is empty, require $m' \le V$). Then the gap encoding of $\ell$ from slot $m$ to $V$ is $m' - m$ copies of the absent-slot block $01$ followed by the gap encoding of $\ell$ from slot $m'$ to $V$.

results.title: Successor of a number with a non-maximal remainder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $0 < d$ and $(c \bmod d) + 1 < d$. Then $\lfloor (c + 1) / d \rfloor = \lfloor c / d \rfloor$ and $(c + 1) \bmod d = (c \bmod d) + 1$.

results.title: Entry label of a literal routine (transition-clause generator)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Among the labels of the generator with $N$ situations and $m$ literal numbers, the entry label of literal $j \in \mathbb{N}$ of situation $i < N$ is the first stage of the routine for literal $j$ of situation $i$ when $j < m$, and the halting label $\mathrm{done}$ when $j \ge m$.

results.title: Label after a literal routine in the transition-family generator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $N$ be the number of situations and $m$ the number of literals per clause, let $i < N$ be a situation and $j$ a natural number. After the routine for literal $j$ of the clause of situation $i$, the generator moves to the label that emits the leading gap of that clause if $j = 0$. Otherwise it moves to the first label of the routine for literal $j - 1$ if $j - 1 < m$, and to the halting label if $j - 1 \ge m$.

results.title: Entry label of the clause routine for situation $i$

results.title: Sum of prefixes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $l$ of pairs $(a, q)$ of a label and a process, the process that chooses among the prefixes $a.q$ listed in $l$: the empty list gives the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$, and the list with head $(a, q)$ and tail $r$ gives the choice $a.q + P$ between the prefix $a.q$ and the process $P$ built in the same way from $r$.

results.title: Transitions of a sum of prefixes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every recursive specification, every list $l$ of pairs of a label and a process, every label $a$ and every process $q$, the sum of the prefixes listed in $l$ has a transition labelled $a$ to $q$ exactly when $(a, q)$ belongs to $l$.

results.title: Realization of a code-level transition system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fix a recursive specification. A family of processes $P_x$ indexed by codes $x$ realizes a function $s$ that lists, for each code $x$, labelled transitions $(a, y)$ with $a$ a label and $y$ a code, when for every code $x$, every label $a$ and every process $q$, the process $P_x$ has a transition with label $a$ to $q$ exactly when $s(x)$ contains an entry $(a, y)$ with $P_y = q$.

results.title: Constants listing their transitions realize them
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix a recursive specification, a map $\iota$ from codes to process constants and a function $s$ listing labelled transitions for each code. Suppose that for every code $x$, writing $(a_1, y_1), \dots, (a_n, y_n)$ for the entries of $s(x)$ in order, the body of the constant $\iota(x)$ is $a_1.\iota(y_1) + (a_2.\iota(y_2) + \dots + (a_n.\iota(y_n) + 0))$, which is $0$ when $n = 0$. Then the processes $\iota(x)$,…

results.title: Code-level parallel composition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given functions $s$ and $t$ listing the labelled transitions of codes $x$ and $y$, the transitions of the pair $(x, y)$ are listed in three blocks: $(a, (x', y))$ for each entry $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$; then $(a, (x, y'))$ for each entry $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$; then $(\tau, (x', y'))$ for each entry $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$ and each entry $(b, y')$ of $t(y)$ whose labels are complementary, that is, one is the input and the…

results.title: Parallel composition preserves realization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix a recursive specification. If the processes $P_x$ realize $s$ and the processes $Q_y$ realize $t$, then the parallel compositions $P_x \mid Q_y$, indexed by pairs $(x, y)$, realize the code-level parallel composition of $s$ and $t$.

results.title: Boolean restriction test
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $L$ of blocked names, the test returns true on a label exactly when the label is the silent action $\tau$, or an input or an output on a name that does not occur in $L$. It is the Boolean form of the condition that restriction by $L$ allows the label.

results.title: Code-level restriction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $L$ of blocked names and a function $s$ listing the labelled transitions of each code, the restricted transitions of a code $x$ are the entries $(a, y)$ of $s(x)$, in order, whose label $a$ is the silent action $\tau$ or an input or an output on a name that does not occur in $L$.

results.title: Restriction preserves realization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix a recursive specification and a list $L$ of blocked names. If the processes $P_x$ realize $s$, then the restricted processes $P_x \setminus L$ realize the code-level restriction of $s$ by $L$.

results.title: Forward certificate check
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s$ list the labelled transitions $(a, x')$ of each implementation code $x$, let $t$ list those of each specification code $y$, and let $R$ be a finite list of code pairs. The forward check succeeds when for every pair $(x, y)$ in $R$ and every entry $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$, either $a = \tau$ and $(x', y)$ is in $R$, or some entry $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$ with the same label has $(x', y')$ in $R$.

results.title: Backward certificate check
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s$ list the labelled transitions $(a, x')$ of each implementation code $x$, let $t$ list those of each specification code $y$, and let $R$ be a finite list of code pairs. The backward check succeeds when for every pair $(x, y)$ in $R$ and every entry $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$, at least one of the following holds: $a = \tau$ and $(x, y')$ is in $R$; some entry $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$ with the same label has $(x', y')$ in…

results.title: Weak-bisimulation certificate check
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For transition lists $s$ of implementation codes and $t$ of specification codes and a finite list $R$ of code pairs, the certificate check succeeds when both the forward check and the backward check succeed on $s$, $t$ and $R$.

results.title: Certificate checks give weak bisimilarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ realize the code-level transition function $s$ and $g$ realize $t$ for a recursive specification, and let $R$ be a list of code pairs on which the certificate check of $s$, $t$ and $R$ succeeds. Then for every pair $(x, y)$ in $R$, the processes $f(x)$ and $g(y)$ are weakly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of the specification.

results.title: Direct check of the root condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given code-level transition functions $s$ on codes $\alpha$ and $t$ on codes $\beta$, each listing labelled steps to codes, a relation $R$ given as a list of code pairs, and codes $x$ and $y$, the root check succeeds exactly when every listed step $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$ is matched by some listed step $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$ with the same label and $(x', y') \in R$, and every listed step $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$ is matched by…

results.title: Certificate checks give rooted observation congruence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ realize the code-level transition function $s$ and $g$ realize $t$ for a recursive specification, and let $R$ be a list of code pairs on which the certificate check of $s$, $t$ and $R$ succeeds. If the root check of $s$, $t$ and $R$ succeeds at codes $x$ and $y$, then the processes $f(x)$ and $g(y)$ are rooted weakly bisimilar (observation congruent) in the labelled transition system of the specification…
